member: Tomas - Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Analyst
message:
Elena, Marcus, Priya, comfort is judged by French footbridge guide (Setra, footbridge vibration guide) and Human-induced Vibration of Steel Structures (HiVoSS, steel footbridge vibration guide) classes in the Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges (E38). Maximum comfort needs below 0.500 m/s² and minimum comfort needs below 1.00 m/s², with above 2.50 m/s² unacceptable, and the 1.90 Hz mode sits inside the critical range so resonance governs.

Elena, Marcus, Priya, the dense crowd at 0.500 pedestrians per square metre in the Vibration Serviceability Assessment of a Historic Suspension Footbridge (E41) with the equivalent-synchronized rule in the 4.4.1 Dynamic load cases guide (E42) gives the dense-crowd resonant force estimate (E50) of 1.48e3 N. The bare-deck acceleration scaling (E51) of 9.26 m/s² is 0.944 times gravity and would almost lift a person, clearly unacceptable, while the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 m/s² is 0.0556 times gravity, like gentle bus braking, below the 1.00 m/s² bound.

Elena, Marcus, Priya, comfort holds without impact jolts because the dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm is thumbnail-scale with 2.49 times margin to plus-minus 50 mm stops in the bolted frame sketch (E37). Ready, because dense-crowd acceleration and clearance now meet minimum comfort with the deck look unchanged.
